title: CAN-FD Sensor/Control Node
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a general-purpose CAN-FD node intended for a 24 V industrial system.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a general-purpose CAN-FD node for a 24 V industrial system.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The controller is a modern MCU that provides CAN-FD.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: for a 24 V industrial system. Use a modern MCU with CAN-FD

fixed_requirements.requirement: The bus physical layer is an external CAN-FD transceiver, i.e. a device separate from the MCU.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: an external CAN-FD transceiver, switchable 120-ohm termination

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board provides 120-ohm bus termination that is switchable, not permanently fitted.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: switchable 120-ohm termination, ESD protection at the bus connector

fixed_requirements.requirement: ESD protection is provided at the bus connector.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: ESD protection at the bus connector, reverse-polarity and transient protection on the 24 V input

fixed_requirements.requirement: The 24 V input has reverse-polarity protection.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: reverse-polarity and transient protection on the 24 V input, and an efficient local regulator.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The 24 V input has transient protection.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: ESD protection at the bus connector, reverse-polarity and transient protection on the 24 V input

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board includes an efficient local regulator. The brief does not state the regulator's input source, topology or output rails.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: and an efficient local regulator. Provide four digital inputs

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board provides four digital inputs.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Provide four digital inputs and four low-side outputs for demonstration loads.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board provides four low-side outputs, intended to drive demonstration loads.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: four low-side outputs for demonstration loads. The CAN connector must place CANH/CANL adjacent

fixed_requirements.requirement: The CAN connector places CANH and CANL on adjacent pins.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The CAN connector must place CANH/CANL adjacent and keep protection/termination near the connector.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Bus protection and termination are placed near the CAN connector.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: adjacent and keep protection/termination near the connector.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Where the brief is silent, the design agent makes and documents reasonable engineering decisions instead of inventing hidden user requirements; stated requirements are authoritative.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic does not accumulate in the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

open_decisions.decision: Which MCU (vendor, family, part number, package, memory, pin count) provides the CAN-FD controller.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks only for 'a modern MCU with CAN-FD' and names no vendor, family, part or package.

open_decisions.decision: Which external CAN-FD transceiver is used, and which of its optional features (silent/standby mode, wake, bus-fault reporting, split/biasing pin) the design relies on.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires an external CAN-FD transceiver but names no device and no feature set.

open_decisions.decision: MCU clock source - internal oscillator, crystal, or oscillator module - its frequency, and the frequency-tolerance budget over temperature and life.
open_decisions.why_open: 'MCU clocking' is listed as a stressor in the metadata, but the brief states no clock source, frequency or tolerance.

open_decisions.decision: Arbitration-phase and data-phase bit rates, sample points and the resulting bit-timing/oscillator-tolerance margin.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no bit rate, bus length, or node count for the CAN-FD network.

open_decisions.decision: How termination is switched (jumper, DIP switch, solder link, electronically controlled) and whether it is a single resistor or split termination with a common-mode capacitor.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes the value as 120 ohm and requires it to be switchable, but does not state the switching mechanism or the termination topology.

open_decisions.decision: Bus ESD protection device class and its ratings - clamping voltage, contact/air discharge level, and line capacitance budget against CAN-FD data-phase edges.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires ESD protection at the bus connector but states no immunity level, device type or capacitance limit.

open_decisions.decision: The 24 V front-end topology: reverse-polarity method (series diode, P-FET, ideal-diode controller), transient clamp choice, fusing or current limiting, and input filtering.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the two protections but not the circuit, the transient energy or surge level to survive, or whether fusing is required.

open_decisions.decision: Regulator topology - linear, switching, or a pre-built module - and, if the chosen topology switches, its switching frequency; plus what 'efficient' means quantitatively for this board and what the regulator's input source is.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief calls for 'an efficient local regulator' with no efficiency target, topology, input source, or load condition stated.

open_decisions.decision: Rail voltages and the current budget for MCU, transceiver, inputs and outputs, including whether the transceiver and MCU share a rail or need separate ones.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no supply rail other than the 24 V input and gives no current budget.

open_decisions.decision: Digital input conditioning: expected input signal type and levels, whether inputs must tolerate 24 V field signals, thresholds, filtering, protection and any isolation.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the quantity (four) but nothing about input levels, source type, isolation or protection.

open_decisions.decision: Low-side output switch type and ratings: the load types the outputs are specified to drive (resistive, lamp, inductive), device technology, voltage/current capability, any turn-off clamping the chosen load type requires, and any diagnostics or short-circuit protection.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the quantity (four) and that the loads are for demonstration, but no load type, current, or voltage.

open_decisions.decision: Connector selection for the CAN bus, the 24 V power input, and the digital I/O - type, pin count, pitch, current rating, keying, and whether power and bus share a connector.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only that CANH and CANL are adjacent on the CAN connector; no connector family, pin count or pinout is stated.

open_decisions.decision: Layer count (2 vs 4), stackup, whether the CANH/CANL pair has a continuous reference plane, and whether it is routed to a controlled differential impedance target.
open_decisions.why_open: The metadata says only '2 or 4' layers; the brief states no stackup, dielectric or impedance requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, keepouts, and any enclosure or rail-mount intent.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on mechanical form entirely, apart from the CAN connector's pin adjacency and the protection/termination placement zone.

open_decisions.decision: Programming/debug interface, firmware update path, and any status indicators or bus-activity/fault LEDs.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief does not mention debug access, bootloading, or indicators.

open_decisions.decision: Whether a bus shield/drain connection, common-mode choke, or dedicated bus filtering is provided, and how the bus reference relates to board ground.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires ESD protection at the connector but says nothing about shielding, common-mode filtering, or grounding scheme.

open_decisions.decision: Operating temperature range, EMC/immunity targets, and whether any compliance regime applies.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives an industrial context but states no environmental range or compliance requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Fabrication and assembly constraints: fab vendor and its process capability, assembly side(s), component-height limits, test points and functional-test hooks.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no manufacturing vendor, process, or test strategy.

open_decisions.decision: Whether the transceiver is inhibited from driving the bus during MCU reset, before firmware is loaded, or until rails have settled - and, if so, by what means and on what justification.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the transceiver but imposes no bus-safety, fail-silent or power-sequencing requirement, so whether such inhibition is needed is the design agent's call.

open_decisions.decision: What board markings and documentation, if any, identify the termination selector state, the 24 V input polarity and the I/O channel numbering.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief imposes no silkscreen, labelling or user-documentation requirement on the board.
